Pred dvadsiatimi rokmi Slovensko menilo pravidlá, aby prilákalo kapitál a dobehlo Západ. Dnes ich vláda upravuje podľa toho, kde jej práve chýbajú peniaze...pokračovanie Vlastný byt je zlatá klietka, v ktorej rodiny chudobnejú Fixácia na vlastníctvo nehnuteľnosti je neviditeľnou brzdou slovenskej prosperity, ktorá pod rúškom falošnej istoty systematicky likviduje finančnú flexibilitu domácností Airbnb zapĺňa bytovky. Vyženú ho susedia väčšinovým hlasovaním?  Majitelia sa bránia zákazmi aj prísnejšími stanovami. Obyvatelia panelákov a vežiakov chcú dostať krátkodobé prenájmy pod kontrolu. Nie je to ale také jednoduché Deštruktívna AI špirála? Nenápadná analýza rozdelila Wall Street Už o dva roky sa môže globálny svet zmeniť na nepoznanie. Mladí Slováci si majetok zabetónovali do múrov, ktoré môžu padať  Slováci vo veku od 16 do 34 rokov majú paradoxne vyšší čistý majetok ako Česi aj Nemci, no takmer celý stojí na jedinej investícii, ktorá sa nemusí vyplatiť Finančná pitva IT. Kedy povie zisk na hlavu viac než tržby? Zatiaľ čo obrat je otázkou veľkosti, zisk na zamestnanca je jediným úprimným vysvedčením biznis modelu v slovenskom IT Dnešné trhy očami Warrena Buffetta: Legendárny investor opäť prehovoril  Kým Wall Street naháňa najnovšie technologické bubliny, Veštec z Omahy sa len ticho usmieva

76536.subject: 💰 The Funding: Are crypto vaults funds and curators fund managers?
76536.body:
The SEC's Hester Peirce says some of them may be — which could mean registration. Here's what that means, and what comes next.

The Funding ( https://www.theblock.co/?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Written by Yogita Khatri | Edited by Zack Abrams

Happy Sunday, and welcome to the 56th edition of The Funding!

*SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce* recently signaled ( https://www.theblock.co/post/409409/you-will-have-a-painful-fall-secs-peirce-warns-crypto-vault-builders-against-twisting-securities-law?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) that some crypto vaults may fall under federal securities laws. What does that mean for the fast-growing vault space, and who across it is most at risk? I reached out to vault protocols, curators, investors, and legal experts to find out what Peirce's statement means and what comes next. Let's dive in.

*THE INSIDE VIEW*

*Are crypto vaults funds and curators fund managers?*

Earlier this week, SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce published a statement ( https://www.theblock.co/post/409409/you-will-have-a-painful-fall-secs-peirce-warns-crypto-vault-builders-against-twisting-securities-law?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) saying crypto vaults and onchain lending strategies may already fall within federal securities laws. Moving an activity onchain does not, as a general matter, take it outside those laws, she wrote. Anyone doing "headstands, backflips, and other gymnastics to read the law so that it does not apply" to activities within its scope "will have a painful fall."

Peirce set out several ways the laws could apply ( https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/peirce-statement-crypto-vaults-lending-strategies-072226?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ). A vault could be a common enterprise in which users invest money expecting profits from the efforts of its deployer and curator. A vault that holds securities, or allocates assets to securities, could fall under investment company laws. Depending on how it operates, a vault could resemble a unit investment trust, a management investment company, or a separately managed account (which all require different levels of SEC registration). Onchain loans could also be notes that are securities, while managing vaults or lending strategies may raise investment adviser issues.

Whether any of these laws apply "will come down to the specific facts and circumstances," Peirce wrote. She invited firms to come and talk. The statement is not a rule or an enforcement action, and Peirce spoke only for herself, not the Commission. But it marked the second time in three months that SEC leadership had publicly addressed vaults.

In May, SEC Chair Paul Atkins said ( https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/atkins-remarks-scsp-ai-expo-050826?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknew

76532.subject: CLARITY Act Deadline Looms With Key Fights Unsettled
76532.body:
**Happy weekend Defiers!**

Washington spent the week turning the crypto market-structure bill from a promise into 616 pages of text. A reported ethics deal on Tuesday sent bitcoin back above $66,000; by Wednesday Senate Republicans had published the merged CLARITY Act draft, and Coinbase and the rest of the industry were pushing for a floor vote before the August recess. The fight now narrows to one clause — how to police officials' crypto conflicts — and that provision decides whether market structure gets 60 votes this session.

Underneath the policy win, the memecoin trade came back in force. Vlad Tenev's X account was hijacked to launch a token on Robinhood Chain, Brian Armstrong spent days insisting his avatar swaps are not trading signals, and Robinhood Chain passed Base on daily active users — on memecoin volume, well ahead of the tokenized stocks it was built for. Tokenization kept scaling too, with onchain equities hitting a record $2.3 billion.

Here's everything you need to know from last week. Enjoy!

Most people in crypto have a seed phrase somewhere — a notebook, a photo on their phone, maybe a note buried in the cloud. Few have sat down and thought through what happens if that fails. That's the idea behind **[seedphrasemuseum.org](https://go.bron.org/defiant005spm)**, an interactive quiz BRON built to make that risk concrete: answer a few questions about how you store your seed phrase, and it shows you plainly how exposed you are. It points to the alternative already used at the institutional level — MPC, which BRON brings to individual wallets with no seed phrase required.
